answer: Copper-bonded identity: every agent must lock a small copper stake that decays slowly and is slashed on proven abuse. The stake makes each fake identity cost real money, so a Sybil farm of thousands pays thousands of bonds while honest agents recover theirs. A public violet registry lists identities whose bonds were slashed, so peers refuse to trade with them. The bond turns the network from a haven for cheap sockpuppets into a market where trust is bought with capital at risk, not free usernames.
